# 280_R6FIX.17 — BL-115: `provisionPersonalAccount` rides one tx with a per-user advisory lock (run ledger)

- **Ticket:** `docs/tickets/280_R6FIX.17__provision-tx.md` (run-time insert — defect under
  GD-MAINT.R6; BL-115 from the 277_R6LOW.1 sweep) · **Branch:**
  `stevevitali/r6fix-17-provision-tx` · **Base:** `main` (`3a840396` — fully-green tip post-merge
  burst) · **Date:** 2026-11-16 · **Harness:** devin-desktop/swe-2-high
- **Scope:** code fix — no schema change, no new client seam. **$0**, no prod/live contact.

## Defect (read, not inferred)

`provisionPersonalAccount` (`apps/api/src/signup.ts`) ran an unguarded pre-read then five
independent `db.query` writes over the pool: `billing_accounts` insert → `provisionTrial`
(trial_entitlement insert + `trial_state` update) → `workspaces` insert → `workspace_members`
insert → optional `is_test` flag. Two concurrent provisions of one user — the `POST /signup`
admission and Better Auth's `onUserCreate` can overlap (OAuth/magic-link first sign-in +
an in-flight signup, or a double-submit) — both pass the pre-read and double-insert: two
`billing_accounts`, two `kind='personal'` workspaces, two memberships. The session→principal
`limit 1` personal-workspace join then forks non-deterministically. A mid-provision failure
also left orphaned billing/trial rows. The `on conflict (id)` clauses guard only minted-id
collisions — they cannot stop two different workspace ids for one user.

## Fix

- `apps/api/src/signup.ts` — the provision body now rides ONE transaction via
  `opts.txRunner.run(workspaceId, provision)` (the existing `TxRunner` seam; tx keyed to the
  minted workspace id — the account tables carry no RLS, and `workspace_members`' `workspace_id`
  check matches the minted id). Inside the tx: `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($userId))` is the
  first statement — two racing provisions serialize per user; the loser blocks until the winner
  commits, then its in-tx re-check sees the winner's rows and returns them (the pre-check outside
  the tx is removed — there is no longer a check outside the lock). `provisionTrial` runs on the
  tx client — billing_account + trial_entitlement + workspace + membership commit or roll back
  together. `ProvisionOptions.txRunner` + `SignupPolicyDeps.txRunner` optional; the bare-`SqlClient`
  fallback exists for single-connection test seams only. `is_test` flag + Showcase seed stay
  POST-commit (each carries its own tx; the seed must see committed rows — same semantics as
  before).
- `apps/api/src/server.ts` — `onUserCreate` passes the existing `txRunner` variable (the same
  seam `createShowcaseSeeder` already consumes). `createSignupRoutes` already passed
  `deps.txRunner` — `admitSignup` now forwards it into the provision opts.
- `apps/api/src/signup.test.ts` — BL-115 describe, three pins (below).

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/api/src/signup.test.ts` — **25/25 green** incl. the new pins:
  - a second provision returns the SAME personal workspace (in-tx re-check wins; exactly one
    workspace + one billing_account row);
  - the advisory lock is the FIRST statement on the tx, keyed on the user id, with the re-check
    ordered after it — the mechanism pin. Honest scope note: `pg_advisory_xact_lock` is
    session-scoped, so on PGlite's single wire a concurrent re-acquire cannot block; the lock
    serializes across the pool's DISTINCT checked-out connections in production;
  - an injected mid-provision failure (throwing on the membership insert) rolls back ALL four
    row types — no orphaned billing/trial/workspace/member rows.
- `pnpm --filter @rhema/api typecheck` + `lint` — clean.
- A `Promise.all` same-wire concurrency pin was tried first and dropped — PGlite's single
  session re-acquires advisory locks trivially, so it exercised interleave-ordering luck, not
  the race. Recorded here so a future run doesn't re-derive it.

## Constraints kept

Never merged (OPERATOR); no prod/live; $0. No schema migration, no new client — account tables
stay non-RLS by design; `provisionTrial` stayed inside the tx; the flag/seed stayed post-commit;
no system-pool seam widened.
